utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. We are assembled for the Status Conference this afternoon. I would ask the court officer to call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon Your Honour, this is case number IT-03-73-PT. The Prosecutor versus Cermak and Markac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tieger. Oh, Ms. Sartorio.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: -- and our case manager is Donnica Henry-Frijlink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour. I appear on behalf of the General Cermak with my co-counsel, Mrs. Jadrinka Slavkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honour, I appear as counsel, Mr. Mikulicic as co-counsel, and our case manager, Vladimir Rendulic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, this is the seventh Status Conference in this case. The accused are on provisional release, I would note, and therefore there is no need for them to appear today. A factor has significantly affected the completion of the pre-trial preparation of this case is a motion of the Prosecutor to join with the Accused Cermak and Markac the Accused Ante Gotovina, and also to amend the indictment. That motion was filed in February of this year. The Bench that was conducting the pre-trial proceedings concerning Gotovina was also assigned to deal with this motion of joinder and the amendment of the indictment. And the final filing was on the 12th of May this year, when the Prosecution filed its reply to submissions that have been filed earlier by the counsel not only for the two accused here, but also for the accused Gotovina. And that followed of course the appointment of counsel to represent Gotovina. Now, the effect of all of that has been to substantially to leave in suspense, for the moment, the question of whether these two accused would continue their preparation with a view to standing trial together, or whether the preparations should now be toward a trial of three accused, Gotovina being the third, and whether there would be, as a consequence of such a joinder, if it's ordered, a difference in the form of indictment. That matter is proceeding before the Gotovina Bench as ordered by the President on the 23rd of February, and the answer to that must await that determination. Against that uncertainty, could I ask first, Ms. Sartario, about the progress of Rule 66(A) disclosure.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. At the last Status Conference a couple of issues came up, and one was the Defence counsel was having difficulty sorting out some of the records, so a week after that Status Conference we did send to them a disclosure log, a complete disclosure log that contained the numbers of the documents and the description so that they would be able to match that list up with the records that they have. And as far as I know that's -- everything is okay in that department; I haven't heard otherwise. In addition, after that Status Conference on the same day we sent to the Defence counsel our proposed reduced Rule 66(A)(ii) witness list, as you know it was quite -- it was quite -- over -- and the list was pared down to 223. That's what we did about a week after the last Status Conference. Since then, of course, we have continued with our ISU researching and our document reviews. We have completed the ISU searches on the names of the three accused, and that yielded approximately 4.000 documents. We're just about through those 4.000 documents, but out of those documents we've already made disclosure of over 200 to Defence counsel. Those are pursuant to Rule 68 and 66. And we are about to embark upon further searching with approximately 200 terms. So we've got to run about another 200 searches, so it obviously it's rolling disclosure, and we'll continue to disclose as the documents are reviewed and identified as being subject to disclosure. In addition, since the last Status Conference we have disclosed seven transcripts of video-recorded interviews. These were interviews that had not been disclosed previously. We are awaiting, however, the transcription and -- of 18 more videotapes. But as they come in, as I stated, we will disclose them as they come in. And we have also disclosed, since the last Status Conference, some translations that have come in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. So the position you are saying, is that there is still the process of Rule 66 disclosure to complete. Rule 68 disclosure, likewise, and still in progress. And in particular there is the completion of the review of the present, some 4.000 items, and further searches are still being made, and then there are the various videos.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I can say that we have disclosed to date all of the Rule 66(A)(ii) witness statements that we are aware of that are on other priority list at this point in time. The new -- the new disclosures of witness statements are videotaped statements of suspect interviews and they will be disclosed pursuant to Rule 66, but they're not necessarily on our witness list. But we believe that this date Defence counsel has statements of all of the witnesses that are on our list that we provided in January.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Prodanovic, have you anything to say about disclosure?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] First of all, we would like to thank the Prosecution for having submitted the list of documents that they provided us already. If you remember, we complained about the EDS system from which we couldn't download the documents, so we can now compare the things that the Prosecution has submitted with what we have been able to download and this has facilitated our work. Whatever else Mrs. Sartario has said is correct, and would I like to thank the Prosecutor's office for keeping up to the dead-lines ordered by you and for the time being we don't any problems with the disclosure of documents that are supposed to be disclosed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. That is a very heartening report. Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, General Markac's Defence does not have anything to add to what my colleague Prodanovic has just said, save for maybe the part that has to do with the translations. As our learned friend has just told us, a lot of the documents have not been translated but we trust that that will be resolved soon. As for the rest we are very happy with the cooperation that we have with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Ms. Sartario, the United Kingdom, how has Rule 70 gone?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. The United Kingdom has finally given us approval to disclose 20 of the 136 documents, but they still have 116 to review and those documents should be on the EDS within seven to 10 days.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Does that mean the 20 or the balance?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That's the 20. Right. We will continue to be in contact with them to move them along and get the final approval on all of the rest of the 116 documents. But in addition, since the last Status Conference we've received approval to disclose 12 documents from one agency and four from another agency and again those, I believe yesterday have gone for putting on to the EDS system, which I understand takes seven to 10 days from the time they're requested from us. And we're still waiting for the clearance of seven documents and 13 videotapes from UN headquarters. Those requests are outstanding. And I would just like to say one thing will the translations, if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: I mention earlier that we've disclosed 203 documents from our ISU searches. My understanding is 197 of those were in both English and B/C/S, and those documents are disclosed pursuant to Rule 66 and 68, and I am not aware of a large amount of translations that we need. So if Defence counsel could be a little bit more specific. Or we could speak after about specific documents, I would be happy to check on the status of those translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Could I leave that counsel to confer at the end of this Status Conference. Thank you for that suggestion, Ms. Sartario. You mentioned Rule 70 disclosure from three agencies other than the U.K. The UN you've identified. The other two, are there further documents still under review by them or does that complete the exercise as far as those two agencies are concerned.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: That completes the exercise as to those two agencies, Your Honour; however, as you know, with the ISU searches when we get in a number of documents, if we identify documents that should be disclosed and they're Rule 70, we will have to send out further requests. And we tend to not send out one document, one request at a time, we tend to wait until we have a batch of documents. But as of this point, the only thing that we are waiting is the seven documents and 13 videotapes from UN headquarters, and the British ones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Do either Defence counsel have anything to add further about Rule 70 disclosure? No. Thank you very much. Agreed facts, Ms. Sartario.

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, I think that as Your Honour may recall we did send out a set of agreed facts last fall and received a response. In response to that, last January, just before our last Status Conference, we sent out a letter to Defence counsel with regard to some of their proposed modifications to the some of the agreed facts that they did not agree to but would agree to with proposed modifications. And I don't -- as far as I know we do not have a response yet from Defence counsel. I have not seen a response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this point we are not sending out any further facts and we have not set out any yet in the Gotovina case. We're waiting for a decision on the joinder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it still the view of Defence counsel that agreed facts really should wait until the joinder issue is resolved?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. We adhere to that position that you yourself supported at the last Status Conference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Well, now, are there any other matters that you would wish to raise, Ms. Sartario?

utterances.speaker: MS. SARTORIO
utterances.text: Not from the Prosecution, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Prodanovic, is there anything other concern that you wish to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. PRODANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: And you, Mr. Separovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. SEPAROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Nothing from us, Your Honour. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Well, that was a very uncomplicated and straightforward Status Conference. I suspect the next one will not be so easy. But by then hopefully it will be possible for all these disclosure issues to be behind us, and it will be clear whether it's to be a two or a three-accused trial. And things will be able then to move with more certainty. I would thank you all for your attendance. And we will now adjourn.

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 5.21 p.m.
